
crash is happening in the `Callable::is_valid()` method.

This might be happening when user opens the recent screen and immediately kills the app.

The focus out signal is sent from the Vulkan render thread, which may be too late in this case.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/94971e1b47f6cc59a6d3845d23f16638d28430bb/platform/android/java/lib/src/main/java/org/godotengine/godot/GodotVulkanRenderView.java#L90-L95

I've seen the same crash on logs for Spooky Express too, so it seems to affect pretty much all Godot 4 games (at least using Vulkan).

While we should see how to work it around on the Android side, I think it's a sign of a bug in Callable or StringName that we get such a crash. The stacktrace basically ends up crashing on the StringName comparison here:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2d53a62898a65ba635efd554b101e033070c784c/core/variant/callable.h#L92-L94

Which then appears to crash in `StringName::operator==` defined as:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2d53a62898a65ba635efd554b101e033070c784c/core/string/string_name.h#L109-L113

So I assume it means that at this point the `_data` of `method` is a stale pointer?

> So I assume it means that at this point the _data of method is a stale pointer?

That's right.

I had discussed this issue with Fredia yesterday, and we are not really sure what's triggering this issue on Android. But yeah it's a crash in callable and would be best to fix there.
I lack knowledge about godot's core codebase and currently at a dead end, so I won't be much help but I'm trying to create a reproduction project.

I bet the issue is the window is being freed before `main_loop_focusout()` is called. Which aligns with Syntaxerror's theory above https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/114800#issuecomment-3733288680

`main_loop_focusout()` gets queued to run on a background thread while the engine probably shuts down. By the time the callback is called, the Window is already gone and the callable is stale

> But so should ~Window be responsible for unregistering those callbacks from DisplayServer?

Probably, but it seems we are in race condition territory now too since we are processing stuff on multiple threads. 

Another option would be to add mutexes before the callbacks are accessed and to check their validity ahead of time

> Edit: Even in single window mode, Popups and *Dialogs are Windows too. Does that mean that any time a Popup is created on Android, it will replace the callbacks in DisplayServerAndroid, and since it doesn't clean after itself we leave things in a broken state?

Whoooooooah

> onActivityPaused

This script should force `onActivityPaused` in a loop (when the HOME button is pressed), tested with the Rift Riff Autoplay version. However, the app is also paused "in-game", and the menu is displayed. After 5 minutes of testing on my Samsung Tab S7 Android 13, no crashes were reproduced.


```sh
#!/bin/bash

PKG="com.adriaandejongh.riftriff"

adb shell monkey -p $PKG -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER 1
sleep 15

while true; do
    echo "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"

    echo "HOME"
    adb shell input keyevent KEYCODE_HOME
    sleep 3

    if adb shell pidof $PKG >/dev/null; then
        adb shell monkey -p $PKG -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER 1
    else
        echo "App CRASH?"
        break
    fi

    sleep 5
done
```

@AdriaandeJongh 
Could you adjust the autoplay version at some point? Remove the in-game pause and let the game resume when it's reactivated; perhaps that would allow us to reproduce a crash more quickly. 

Are you also familiar with SH-Script and could you try it on your "weak" Mali G52 device?
For the record, this issue is reproducible in all Godot apps, including the Godot Editor, so that one can be used too to try to reproduce it.

renderer), via Google Play vitals — so a 4.7.x cherry-pick of #121670 / #121146
would still have an audience.

Another **shipped game** data point, seconding the request above for a **4.7.x cherry-pick** of #121670 / #121146.

Still reproducing on **4.7.stable.official** (`5b4e0cb0f`, official `template_release`, arm64-v8a, Mobile/Vulkan renderer), measured through the Play Developer Reporting API rather than the Console UI.

**Scale (last 28 days, one game, ~1,000 DAU):** this exact path accounts for **39 distinct users across 3 clusters** — ~12% of all crashing users, our second-largest crash family after #115170. Both the focus-**out** and focus-**in** variants appear, on app versions spanning our entire release history (version codes 20 → 37), so it is not tied to any one build of ours.

| cluster | users | app versions | entry point |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 22 | 20 → 37 | `main_loop_focusout()` |
| B | 10 | 10 → 37 | `main_loop_focusin()` |
| C | 7 | 23 → 37 | `main_loop_focusout()` |

Devices are ordinary low/mid-range handsets, not one vendor: LIFEPHONE HERO (Android 14), Motorola moto g96 5G (Android 14), Redmi A5. This matches @akien-mga's note that it affects essentially every Vulkan Godot 4 app.

Not asking to reopen — the fix is merged for 4.8. Just adding weight to the 4.7.x backport request, since 4.7.x is still receiving patch releases and this is a measurable, user-visible crash for anyone shipping on it today.
